title: Poonawalla Fincorp Ltd - 524000 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp Q1 FY27 PAT rose 20.8% QoQ to ₹308 crores, ROA 1.98%, GNPA down to 1.37%, AUM ₹67,054 crores (+11% QoQ).
summary.overview: AUM grew 11.1% QoQ to ₹67,054 crores, with retail products driving growth and new products reaching 26% of disbursements. Profitability improved: PAT ₹308 crores (+20.8% QoQ, +391.5% YoY), ROA 1.98% (up 17 bps QoQ), and pre-provisioning operating profit ₹785 crores (+12.9% QoQ). Asset quality improved on all measured metrics, with GNPA at 1.37% (vs 1.44% in Q4), NNPA at 0.70%, and quarterly credit cost at 2.4% (vs 2.51%). Management attributed margin gains to a ~50 bps rise in disbursement yield from product mix, and guided to a June 2028 exit ROA of 3-3.5%.

financial_highlights.metric: Net interest income incl. fees and other income

segments.name: Prime personal loans
segments.commentary: Monthly disbursements reached ₹537 crores at quarter end vs ~₹440 crores in Q4; 38% of disbursements fully straight-through digital, up from 33% in Q4.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Q1 disbursements ~₹875 crores vs ₹890 crores in Q4; 460 branches, with ~400 more planned in FY27 mainly Tier 2/3; LTV 75%.

segments.name: Consumer durables
segments.commentary: Q1 disbursements ₹433 crores; 17,300+ retail outlets across 339 locations; 58,000+ cases disbursed in a single month.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Monthly disbursement ~₹104 crores at June end; channel partners up to 1,100+ from 900; 70+ locations across 30 states.

segments.name: Education loans
segments.commentary: Disbursements up 55% QoQ in Q1, average monthly disbursement ₹144 crores; origination locations expanded from 25 to 50; ~30% of sanctions processed digitally.

segments.name: Business loans / shopkeeper loans
segments.commentary: Business loans growing ~15-16%; shopkeeper loans deliberately not being accelerated given credit cost and ROA considerations.

guidance_outlook: Management guides to a June 2028 exit ROA of 3% to 3.5%, versus 1.98% today.
Opex to AUM may fluctuate 10-25 bps QoQ due to investment and clustered gold branch openings; internal benchmark trends lower over FY27.
Management expects disbursement yield gains to offset any cost of borrowing uptick; no NIM pressure seen at current trajectory.
Gold branch addition of ~400 in FY27, similar to last year's pace; 60 branches already opened this financial year.
Write-offs expected to stay around ₹275-280 crores per quarter run-rate, with no material legacy-book write-offs left.
Management is comfortable on capital for the next 4-5 quarters after the ₹2,500 crore QIP; no further raise indicated.
Provision coverage expected to remain range-bound, with rising gold and education loan share lowering overall PCR over time.
capex_capacity: 460 gold loan branches; plan to add ~400 in FY27, targeting new states including Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Madhya Pradesh.
Consumer durables capacity to process ~50,000 customers a month, per management.
Education loan origination footprint expanded from 25 to 50 locations; consultant network of 600+ partners.
AI estate: 101 AI projects across 21 departments (50 deployed, 51 in pipeline); ~130 smart agents live in production.
demand_pricing: Disbursement yield up ~50 bps QoQ on product mix; portfolio yield up ~17-19 bps; management cites pricing power in prime PL and digital channels.
New products accounted for 26% of disbursements in Q1 vs 24% in Q4 and 20% in the quarter before.
Management says it will slow growth in products where calibration needs it; business loans being grown only to 10-16% levels versus over 40% in used cars.
Retail loan exposure industry-wide grew over 16% YoY as of March 2026; Q1 FY27 cumulative GST collections up 8.4% YoY.
6 MoB 30+ on Q1 sourcing at 0.64%, vs 1.05% in Q4 and 1.66% in Q3FY25 (as stated by management).

qa_highlights.question: Chintan Shah (ICICI Securities): With ROA up ~130 bps YoY to 1.98% and opex/AUM near 4%, what are the next ROA levers, and how much further can credit cost fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to NIM expansion over the last 12 months and disbursement yield up ~50 bps QoQ (after ~40 bps last quarter) from product mix; portfolio yield up ~17-19 bps. Credit cost at 2.4% is expected to keep improving QoQ for a couple of quarters. Opex/AUM may rise 15-25 bps on branch clustering, but structurally should decline over a year. Guidance is a June 2028 exit ROA of 3-3.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Chintan Shah: Secured mix is about 53% against a 50:50 guidance, so is the rise in disbursement yield coming from product mix or from moving into higher-yield segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said business loans are growing only ~15-16%. Prime PL digital share is 36-38% and rising, and digital is priced at a premium. Gold, education and unsecured (Prime PL) are driving yield; portfolio yield on gold is about to reach roughly ₹1,700-1,900 crores scale.

qa_highlights.question: Chintan Shah: Having raised ₹2,500 crores against a ₹5,500 crore approval, will there be a further capital raise this year?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹2,500 crore QIP was raised in early April 2026. Management said it is comfortable for the next 4-5 quarters and will reassess; the focus is on structural strength rather than further raising.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal (Motilal Oswal): Are early delinquency trends in PL, business loans, LAP and CV showing any caution, given peer reports of early bounces among IT-sector salaried borrowers in South India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no emerging stress: 6-MoB 30+ for the latest sourcing is 0.64% vs 1.05% in Q4; Stage 3 slippage improved ~13% and Stage 1 slippage ~5% QoQ; bounce rates are stable to lower; collection efficiency is ~99.6%.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal: Among the six newer businesses, which has surprised positively and which has scaled slower, and has strategy changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shopkeeper loans are the only product not being accelerated, given credit cost and ROA considerations. Gold has 460 branches with ~60 opened this fiscal. Education loans are around ₹144 crores monthly. CV and CD early vintages are performing better than historical data. Management also said agri and microfinance are not in the book.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal: Cost of borrowing rose ~9 bps QoQ, so will it keep inching up?
qa_highlights.answer: Arvind Kapil said the increase is not a concern, citing NCDs at 25-30% of funding and a diversified borrowing mix. He said disbursement yield rose 50 bps this quarter after 40 bps last quarter, and the company should remain NIM accretive. No formal guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Pranay Mehta (Investec): What growth and profitability can be expected over the next 8-10 quarters, and are more new products coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the June 2028 exit ROA guidance of 3-3.5% from 1.98% today. It cited rising yields and better credit cost via calibration and collections. No specific new product launch was detailed.

qa_highlights.question: Pranay Mehta: Are NBFCs reporting stress in IT-sector distribution, and what is the company's view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the six-product mix spans different economic cycles. Business loans are held at ~10-16% growth versus over 40% in used cars, and it will slow products where calibration needs it. It is watchful of macro indicators, and agri and microfinance are not in the book.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint (Kotak): Is the quarterly write-off run-rate of about ₹275-280 crores recurring, or is there a legacy element?
qa_highlights.answer: Shriram Iyer said write-offs have declined QoQ, the legacy portfolio is now immaterial, and write-offs should not rise. He confirmed ₹275-280 crores as the run-rate for the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint: Is the fall in PCR (Stage 2 coverage near 18%) normalised, and what is the cost of funding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PCR is range-bound and is driven by product mix; the legacy high-ECL book has run off, and gold and education loan share increases will lower PCR over time. Sanjay Miranka said a small cost-of-funds uptick is possible but disbursement yield gains should offset it, with no NIM challenge seen. Gold LTV is 75%.

risks_watch: Opex/AUM may move 10-25 bps QoQ from gold branch clustering (~400 branch adds planned in FY27), which could offset ROA gains.
Cost of borrowing rose to 7.72% from 7.63%; management says disbursement yield gains will offset it, but no formal guidance was given.
Early-warning signals in salaried and IT-sector borrowers flagged by peers; management says none seen internally, so monitor 6-MoB 30+ and bounce rates next quarter.
Credit cost of 2.4% and write-offs of ₹275-280 crores per quarter must hold for the ROA trajectory; PCR is expected to remain range-bound.
Shopkeeper loans are deliberately held back, and business loans are growing only 10-16%, so the growth mix depends on prime PL, gold and education scaling.
Macro risk: management cites crude oil and fuel-price pressure on CVs and watches industry-wide retail stress; the 2028 exit ROA target of 3-3.5% depends on execution.
key_quotes: Our GNPA, which in finance companies, we do believe is a lead indicator , the GNPA for Q1 FY27 stands at 1.37% versus 1.44% in Q4FY27.
We did not just launch 6 businesses. We built 6 growth engines mounted on a single chas sis. That's important.
So write-offs have been reducing quarter -on-quarter and control over slippages because of the better collection efficiency.
So we don't see any challenge at NIM level.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on margins, asset quality and the 2028 ROA target, with management repeatedly describing the trajectory as structural. Cautious on opex/AUM (conservative 10-25 bps swings flagged) and deflects the IT-sector and cost-of-funds questions to data rather than offering firm guidance.

adds.what: ~400 gold loan branches planned in FY27, mainly Tier 2/3 (new states incl. UP, AP, Telangana, MP); 60 already opened this FY
Education loan origination locations expanded from 25 to 50 (already expanded)

growth.why: Management guides ROA exit of 3–3.5% by June 2028 (vs 1.98% today) and ~400 new gold branches in FY27 (60 opened so far), with AUM up 11.1% QoQ and disbursement yield up ~50 bps on mix; no explicit revenue growth figure given and the ROA target is a profitability guide rather than a revenue number.
